BackstoryDef.title: street brawler
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up fighting. Not for pleasure, though it was that too, but because the alternative was losing. [PAWN_pronoun] learned early that the trick was not to hit harder than anyone, but to take a hit better. By the time [PAWN_pronoun] was old enough to be recruited, [PAWN_possessive] hands already knew what they were for.

BackstoryDef.title: stablehand
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in the stables serving a minor lord's estate, hauling feed and mending tack. The hired swords who passed through never seemed especially impressive up close, but [PAWN_nameDef] watched how they moved and remembered everything. When the estate folded and the work dried up, [PAWN_pronoun] already knew which guild hall to walk into.

BackstoryDef.title: guild fighter
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has been carrying guild contracts for years: pest control in summer, escorted caravans in autumn, debt collection whenever the weather is bad enough that no one will be outside to watch. [PAWN_pronoun] does not take every contract, has turned down a few on principle, and has never missed a filing deadline. The Guildmaster considers [PAWN_objective] reliable, which is the guild's highest compliment.

BackstoryDef.title: guild veteran
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] has been at this long enough to have their name on the public board in three different chapter halls. Most of the contracts [PAWN_pronoun] takes now are flagged as difficult or declined by everyone else. [PAWN_pronoun] does not particularly enjoy the work but is very good at it, and the guild pays well for people who come back.

BackstoryDef.title: guild champion
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] holds the rank of Champion, the highest the Guild gives to someone still taking field contracts. The rank did not come through seniority or politics but through a very specific and well-documented series of completed assignments that the regional guildmaster eventually ran out of excuses not to recognize. [PAWN_pronoun] is not famous in the way heroes are famous. [PAWN_pronoun] is famous in the way reliable tools are famous: slowly, quietly, and mostly among the people who need them most.
